Parallel Gateway

General Concept: A Parallel Gateway in BPMN is used to model parallel execution, where all outgoing paths are taken simultaneously. It is used for forking and joining parallel flows.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, Parallel Gateways synchronize incoming and outgoing flows. The engine ensures all required paths are completed before continuing. Variable scoping and input mappings can be used to provide data for parallel execution.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
A Parallel Gateway in TaktX allows you to:

  • Synchronize incoming and outgoing flows for concurrent process execution.
  • Split process flow into multiple parallel paths or join them together.
  • Use input mappings to provide data for parallel execution.
  • Configure error handling for missing or incomplete paths.
  • Monitor gateway synchronization and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for concurrent activities and workflow synchronization points.

 

Example: Parallel Checks with Parallel Gateway

 

This example shows a process where a Parallel Gateway splits work into two parallel tasks (Background Check and Credit Check) and then joins before process completion. This demonstrates concurrent execution and synchronization in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use parallel gateways for concurrent activities.
  • Document the logic for synchronization points.
  • Test gateway behavior with different input data.

Pitfalls:

  • Missing or incomplete paths can block process progress.
  • Unmapped variables may lead to incorrect execution.
